topic: Madras HC: a worker's death from work pressure or heavy work can be a death 'in the course of employment' under Section 3(1), Employees' Compensation Act, 1923 - no external injury needed; employment need not be the only cause if work contributed to or hastened death; 51-year-old cotton-loading helper at a Theni textile mill collapsed with stress and BP on 16 Nov 2016, brought dead; Commissioner's award of Rs 5,32,800 (insurer Rs 3 lakh under group personal accident policy, mill Rs 2,32,800) with 12% interest under Section 4A(3) upheld; insurer's appeal dismissed (The Branch Manager v. N. Pitchaimani & Anr., CMA (MD) No. 619 of 2023, 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 562, Justice P. Murugan, Madurai Bench, reported 25 Nov 2026)

slides.title: Died from **work pressure**? Family can claim.
slides.subtitle: A worker's death caused by **heavy work and stress** can count as a death during employment, even with **no visible injury**.
slides.cite: **The Branch Manager v. N. Pitchaimani** · CMA (MD) No. 619 of 2023 · 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 562 · Justice P. Murugan

slides.label: What happened
slides.title: Collapsed while **loading cotton**
bullets: A **51-year-old helper** loaded cotton at a textile mill in **Theni**, Tamil Nadu, earning **Rs 300 a day**.
On **16 November 2016**, she suffered **stress and high BP** from heavy work, fainted, and was declared **brought dead** at hospital.
Her family claimed compensation. The **Commissioner** awarded **Rs 5,32,800** with **12% yearly interest**.

slides.label: The insurer's objection
slides.title: "Not an accident," said the **insurer**
bullets: The mill had a **group personal accident policy** covering up to **Rs 3 lakh** per worker. The insurer was told to pay that part.
It argued there was **no external injury** and she already had BP and stress, so this was a **normal death**, not an accident.
The mill was told to pay the remaining **Rs 2,32,800**.

slides.label: What the Court said
slides.title: Work strain **counts**
bullets: She died **during her employment**, because of **work pressure and heavy work**. That falls under **Section 3(1)** of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923.
**No visible injury** is not a reason, by itself, to reject a claim. Work need not be the **only cause** if it contributed to or hastened death.
The **12% interest** follows **Section 4A(3)**. The insurer's appeal was **dismissed**.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: What this ruling **does not** mean
bullets: It does **not** mean every death of a worker is automatically covered. The link between the **work** and the death must be shown on facts.
Families should keep **wage proof, duty records and medical papers**, and file the claim before the **Commissioner**.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
Can a death from work pressure be treated like a workplace accident? The Madras High Court says yes 🏭⚖️

A 51-year-old helper loading cotton at a textile mill in Theni collapsed on 16 November 2016 after stress and high blood pressure from heavy work. She was declared brought dead. The Commissioner awarded her family Rs 5,32,800 with 12% yearly interest: Rs 3 lakh from the insurer under the mill's group accident policy, the rest from the mill.

The insurer appealed. It said there was no external injury and she already had BP, so this was a normal death, not an accident. Justice P. Murugan disagreed. She died during her employment because of work pressure and heavy work, which is covered by Section 3(1) of the Employees' Compensation Act, 1923. The lack of a visible injury alone cannot defeat the claim.

The Court upheld the award and the 12% interest under Section 4A(3), and dismissed the appeal. Remember, each case depends on its facts, and the link between the work and the death must be shown.

Case: The Branch Manager v. N. Pitchaimani & Anr., CMA (MD) No. 619 of 2023, 2026 LiveLaw (Mad) 562
Court: Madras High Court, Madurai Bench, Justice P. Murugan
